Before UP (from initial state):
- Node 4: color=c (charcoal), pixels=12, boundary=[[28, 28], [28, 39], [31, 39], [31, 28]], children=[6]

- Node 9: color=W (white), pixels=4, boundary=[[48, 32], [48, 35]]
- Node 10: color=N (green), pixels=12, boundary=[[49, 32], [49, 35], [51, 35], [51, 32]]
After UP:
- Node 4: color=b (blue), pixels=28, boundary=[[28, 28], [28, 39], [31, 39], [31, 28]]
- Node 6: color=g (gray), pixels=20, boundary=[[29, 29], [29, 38], [30, 38], [30, 38]]
- Node 9: color=W (white), pixels=4, boundary=[[44, 32], [44, 35]]
- Node 10: color=N (green), pixels=12, boundary=[[45, 32], [45, 35], [47, 35], [47, 32]]
Key changes:
1. Node 4 changed from charcoal (c) to blue (b) - the horizontal bar changed color!
2. Node 9 (white) moved from row 48 to row 44 (moved up by 4)
3. Node 10 (green) moved from rows 49-51 to rows 45-47 (moved up by 4)
So the green target zone moved up! The horizontal bar also changed from charcoal to blue.
This is interesting - it seems like the green target area is moving up, and the bar changed color. Let me think about what this means...
Actually, wait. The bar (node 4) was charcoal with gray inside before, now it's blue with gray inside. And the green target moved up.
Let me try more UP presses to see if the green target continues moving up toward the blue squares.
